question: Which RF-cycle-resolved state variables differ when native eduPIC sustains more above-15.8-eV field-push traffic than AuroraPIC?

basis.observed_before_declaration: Frozen mover, collision-rate, and collision-product audits found no large direct operator discrepancy. Two AuroraPIC branches close species balance exactly and show 0.44--2.64 percent gross creation/loss dispersion, while their pooled promotion deficit remains 16--20 percent relative to native.

gates.passivity: every final checkpoint must equal its previously locked passive native checkpoint hash
gates.balance: electron and ion population changes must equal ionization minus corresponding wall losses at every cycle
gates.channel_closure: electron elastic plus excitation plus ionization counts must equal total electron collisions
gates.native_repeatability: three-seed relative range no greater than 8 percent for four-cycle normalized ionization, loss, energetic-fraction, kinetic-energy, and field-energy metrics
gates.finite_and_physical: all numeric values finite and nonnegative except signed population increments

interpretation.gross_traffic_difference: supported if native/Aurora normalized ionization or wall-loss traffic differs from unity by at least 10 percent with all gates passing
interpretation.energetic_occupancy_difference: supported if native/Aurora final energetic fraction differs from unity by at least 10 percent with all gates passing
interpretation.bulk_energy_or_field_difference: supported if native/Aurora same-phase kinetic or field energy differs from unity by at least 10 percent with all gates passing
interpretation.unresolved_if: all compared ratios remain within 10 percent; the next test must match a portable particle state across implementations rather than compare independently evolved states

claim_boundary: This prospectively adds cycle-resolved native state diagnostics to an existing one-case code comparison. Native and AuroraPIC states are independently evolved, so the result can identify differing observables but cannot assign causal onset to one algorithm or validate experiment.
